latest_substantive_result.summary: The producer return reports that, in a specified large-assembly rotor model with opposing nonwinding contacts, fueling lowers one mode variance by 0.81%, raises static compliance by 6.36%, and yields Var/(Tχ)=0.93260 on the same attached assembly; a separate mode-bath heat calculation reports +0.00799 into the device. Mode transfer is O(1) against O(M) fuel use, so this does not establish efficient bulk cooling.

next_decisive_step: No automatic follow-up is implied. If this route is explicitly resumed, the decisive acquisition is a molecularly grounded contact and chemical-kinetic model with complete bath/work accounting, tested against the established cooling comparators.

limitations: The stable balanced branch, rapid bending equilibration, large assembly, proportional support scaling and specified chemical landscape are model assumptions; the coupled rotor-flap contact and molecular kinetic landscape are not acquired.
The source preserves failures in the freely moving follower, alternative chemical barrier and excessively flexible contact variants; these constrain the proposed mechanism.
The mode heat output is O(1) while fuel use is O(M); neither efficient bulk cooling nor a complete practical device advantage is established.
Electronic feedback cooling and continuous thermal-pawl mechanisms remain strong comparators; novelty, priority and practical superiority are UNKNOWN.
